pr_title: Extend speed testing to provider-based sig and kem algorithms
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/19535

Open question: Can someone please point me to documentation for "MR" output to meet expectations? Currently the implementation of this based on "surrounding code" :-/
pr_comments:
> Can someone please point me to documentation for "MR" output to meet expectations? Currently the implementation of this based on "surrounding code" :-/

Unfortunately there is no documentation.

> Unfortunately there is no documentation.

Alright. Then this is ready for review.
Could you please squash the commits into one or two commits?

> Could you please squash the commits into one or two commits?

So done: Thanks for checking that this is as you'd expect it.

> Fixes #19535
> 
> Open question: Can someone please point me to documentation for "MR" output to meet expectations? Currently the implementation of this based on "surrounding code" :-/

`mr` means _machine-readable_  resultats. 

`mr` flag is explicitly set to 1, inside forked process.

It is used to format forked child process results into stdout pipe, to send them send back to the parent process, who will parse and store them.

Search and follow the `"+F2:` string, you will understand the mechanism.

In your case, as you have separated results arrays (`kems_results`, `sigs_results`) , you need to implement a "+F9:"  and "+F10:" keywords processing ( or "+FA:" if hex value can be handled easily, i bet so).

speed fork mode is activated using the `-multi n` option

> Search and follow the `"+F2:` string, you will understand the mechanism.

Thanks for the suggestion: I got it now. Please check again, @FdaSilvaYY .

Also changed in this iteration initiated by your suggestion for re-factoring:
- One algorithm can now be tested in multiple setups: Most notable is the RSA "family" in both sign/verify as well as encaps/decaps.
- Such as to also enable keygen testing in line with all other algorithms, the DSA "family" was changed from 512-2048 to 1024-3072 bits to be in line with the parameter limitations in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/43a9e682d80d0abe4ffd0c76d18c43cf059a2bcc/crypto/ffc/ffc_params_generate.c#L42-L64

> A few more nits. Have you push your last commits ? cause I don't see the fixes you mention in this PR.

Yes, I did. Admittedly, I overlooked (removing) quite a few parentheses :( Now done. I also reverted the DSA 3k addition and will do a separate PR (as it also requires adding a key in another file).

@FdaSilvaYY @t8m Can I ask whether one of you waits for something from my side to (re)review this? Together with #19312 (thanks again, @mattcaswell for moving that forward!) this would allow us to focus on oqs-provider as the default mechanism for PQC TLS embedding (selfish motivation: saving effort maintaining the oqs-openssl111 fork).

@FdaSilvaYY Thanks again for the review. All suggestions are now incorporated in the latest commit. Please mark conversations resolved where/if you agree. Please also let me know which next steps I should take to move this forward.
@t8m Thanks for the review. Please check the latest commit correctly addresses all your suggestions.

@t8m Thanks for the approval. 
@FdaSilvaYY @mattcaswell Can I please ask you to provide a second approval to move this forward towards merge? We'd like to "advertise" this feature to allow anyone to do simple performance comparisons of PQ algorithms. Thanks in advance.

issue_context.title: openssl speed support for provider-based kem and signature algorithms
issue_context.body: Is the understanding correct that neither KEM (encaps/decaps) nor signature (sign/verify) algorithms implemented in providers can be triggered/tested via [openssl speed](https://www.openssl.org/docs/manmaster/man1/openssl-speed.html)? If so, would a PR be welcome to add such feature?
comments: Yes, such a PR would be welcomed.

review_comments: Please add empty line after declarations.

You better add a few tests here to determine and store an value from an `enum kem_type_t { RSA_KEM = 1, EC_KEM, X25519, X448 }`
and so you can simplify the next calls to `strncmp`
Ah, that's how you'd like to see it. Will change as proposed.

This value is stored, but it is never tested or displayed , no ?
you better discard it.  

This structure contains the contexts and just enough information to run each operation.
It is not used to store any result or intermediate value.

All values above are required during processing of the actual performance loops, e.g., `out_len` above allows  (correct) operation of `EVP_PKEY_encapsulate(ctx, out, &out_len, secret, &secret_len);`. Or am I overlooking something there (or in your comment)?
